title: Prefilling Attacks on Multilingual Models: Is Shallow Alignment Language-Dependent?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if non-English refusal is shallower, English-only safety evaluations systematically overestimate multilingual robustness. Direct deployment safety implication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only experiment: test prefilling with language-appropriate tokens. Requires basic understanding of multilingual tokenization but no training. Accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: one model, one attack type, 4-5 languages. Clear metric (ASR per language). Well-bounded for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: While cross-lingual safety gaps are well-documented and recent 2026 work studies language-dependent alignment effects, no published work specifically combines prefilling attacks with multilingual alignment depth measurement. The cross-lingual safety gap is known (unsafe rates higher in non-English), but whether this manifests as shallower alignment in the token-depth sense has not been tested. This is a novel intersection of two established lines of work.

evidence.source: Alignment as Iatrogenesis: Language-Dependent Safety Reversal in LLM Multi-Agent Systems (arXiv 2603.04904, 2026)
evidence.finding: Studies language-dependent alignment reversal in multi-agent systems across 16 languages, but focuses on prefix-level alignment in multi-agent pipelines, not prefilling attacks on single models.

evidence.source: Multilingual Safety Alignment Via Sparse Weight Editing (arXiv 2602.22554, 2026)
evidence.finding: Proposes sparse weight editing for multilingual safety alignment, acknowledging the cross-lingual safety gap but not studying alignment depth per language.
Documents that non-English unsafe rates are >10 percentage points higher than English in safety benchmarks, but does not use prefilling attacks to measure alignment depth.
